item.title: Spurs forward withdraws from national team duty due to injury worry
item.description: Spurs forward withdraws from national team duty due to injury worry Tottenham forward Mathys Tel has withdrawn from the France Under-21 squad after suffering an injury in Saturday’s 1-0 defeat to Leeds United. Tel was forced off at Elland Road after being on the receiving end of a strong challenge from Jayden Bogle, with Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi admitting afterwards that he feared a significant problem. “Bad injury, and now we have to make the medical check,” De Zerbi said following the game. The French Football Federation confirmed on Monday that Tel will not join up with the Under-21 squad as a result of the injury. That means the forward will miss France’s upcoming fixtures against Italy and England. A statement from the FFF read: “Having suffered an injury with his club Tottenham, Mathys Tel is forced to withdraw from the France Under-21 team training camp which began this Monday at the CNF Clairefontaine.” Stay up to date with all the latest Spurs news by joining our Tottenham WhatsApp channel .

item.description: Michigan football pulled the plug on offensive coordinator Jason Beck ; now the questions really start. How will offensive line coach Jim Harding, promoted to interim OC for the remainder of the season, change the scheme? Will there be less "rhino" personnel calls? Will he get Tony Alford to shrink the running back rotation? Will he look for new ways to attack downfield? Will there be a commitment to more interior running? While those answers remain unknown, the one thing that seems to be understood is that this offense can not be entirely reinvented in just five days midseason. WHY IT HAPPENED: Kyle Whittingham didn't plan to fire Jason Beck. Then he turned on MSU tape "You can't do major changes at this juncture, and so it will be collaborative," coach Kyle Whittingham said Monday, Nov. 9, at his weekly media availability. "It had been collaborative. I mean, it's never just a one-man show, but you know you can only do so much at this point in the season, and there'll be a few different wrinkles for sure. "But to say there's going to be a complete overhaul, that's not really feasible." Harding has shared offensive coordinator at two stops in his career (2015-16 at Utah, 2013 at Idaho) but has never been in charge of play-calling. Whittingham said there weren't a ton of proven play-callers on offense on his staff, but opted to tab Harding because "he's been with me for a lot of years now, and to me, he was the right fit and the right guy to get through these three weeks of the season." Although most of the Wolverines ' hopes have been wiped away, the plan is not to make Harding the long-term solution for the offense, but instead a bandage to help the Wolverines get their sixth win and avoid missing the postseason for the first time since 2014. OTHER ISSUES: Michigan's offense stinks, but what happened to defense, special teams? U-M is also already doing damage control for its future, as Whittingham said he and the staff called "every recruit" Sunday to discuss the direction moving forward. He called the reaction "receptive and positive," adding that his vibe was that "nobody was panicking." He also said a single coach isn't the only reason for recruits to choose Michigan. “First of all, it’s Michigan," he said. "You come to Michigan for a lot of reasons: academics, the tradition, the history. Coaching changes are a part of college football. They go on constantly. There’s been several coordinator changes, head coach changes so far this year, and there’s going to be a lot more, I can tell you that. That’s just part of the deal. item.title: Jupiter swimming and diving wins first-ever state championship
item.description: Jupiter boys swimming and diving has completed its "dream" season with the most coveted of state hardware. The Warriors' program won its first-ever state championship, pacing the pool across Class 4A to finish first at the podium on Saturday, Nov. 7. Jupiter outlasted runner-up Cypress Bay by 5.5 points to take home gold, with the competition coming down to the very last event. The Warriors team swam the 400 yard relay with a time of 3:01.30, edging the second-place Lightning in the event as well as the total team score. "It was an incredible, historical moment for Jupiter High School because this is the first time we're winning the championship title with the boys," head coach Kiril Zahariev said. Jupiter paced the field with 206.5 points, followed by Cypress Bay with 201, Winter Park with 186.5, Nease with 153, and Riverview Sarasota with 143 to round out Florida's top five across Class 4A. FHSAA football playoff bracket release: 5 Palm Beach County takeaways Wellington transfer Julian Granison and Charles "Buddy" Howard shared the honors of "MBS" as Zahariev puts it ― "most valuable swimmer." Granison, a Florida commit, won the 50-yard (19.50, a personal best) and 100-yard frees (42.86, a personal best) events, while Howard, a Michigan commit, took first place in the 200-yard free (1:36.70, a personal best) and 100-yard fly (48.15) events. Chase Young and Asher Smith also participated in the winning 400-yard free relay team, while Slater Woodard helped the Warriors win the 200 free relay. The Warriors boys program boasted six seniors this season, with all coming together to finish their respective high school careers on top with the state title. "It was an amazing performance by all the kids," Zahariev said. "We are so blessed with the title." On the Jupiter girls' side, NC State commit Veronica Metz won the 200 free in a time of 1:45.68, helping the Warriors to a fourth-place finish. Boca Raton junior Caleb Caponera also shined for the Bobcats' boys program with two titles. He swam a 1:46.57 in the 200 IM and a 55.71 in the 100 breast. Alex Peterman is a high school sports reporter for The Palm Beach Post. He can be reached at apeterman@usatodayco.com. item.title: Greg Sankey addresses impact of midterms on Protect College Sports Act: 'Elections have consequences'
item.description: Six days after the midterm elections, the House of Representatives was due to report back to Washington, D.C. on Monday after the recess. It will be a lame-duck session of Congress, though, after both the Democrats took control of both the House and Senate. As a result, there’s a level of uncertainty around the Protect College Sports Act as legislators return from the break. The bipartisan bill advanced out of the Senate by a 77-22 vote , but the House was not in session and lawmakers did not return from the campaign trail to take it up. $39.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage Now, they’re back in Washington, D.C., but questions remain. SEC commissioner Greg Sankey realizes that and said he expects plenty of action this week, and the conference is in communication with members of Congress. “We had an election last week and elections have consequences, as they say,” Sankey said on The Paul Finebaum Show . “I think our Senators and House of Representatives members are returning to D.C. probably as we speak. I’m certain it will be an active week in many different ways.” SUBSCRIBE to the On3 NIL and Sports Business Newsletter All told, more than 25 incumbent Republican members of the House of Representatives lost to Democrats in their respective races. Democrats have gained more than 40 seats in the House, according to NBC News , and took the Senate by at least four seats. That means Congress will be returning for a lame-duck session, and as Ross Dellenger reported for On3, it impacts the Protect College Sports Act’s future . While there are questions about what exactly could lie ahead for the bill, there’s concern about attendance and how many Republicans return to work after losing their seats. Sankey knows about the level of uncertainty for the bill in the weeks ahead. But he made clear college sports leaders have to be ready for whatever happens, whether the bill passes the House or if it doesn’t. “As I understand, the House has some leadership decisions to make on a move-forward basis,” Sankey said. “We’ve communicated with current leadership our position. How that might move forward, given the changes that are coming, is a question mark. How we think as a league and with our colleagues is where can we provide clarity, as I mentioned, in this time of uncertainty on key issues? Some of those are embedded in the Protect College Sports Act. “The reaction is we’ll see what comes out of the D.C. over the next few weeks. They have to fund the government … and any number of other important issues. But we’ll have to prepare with or without the PCSA.” Greg Sankey: Congress must help set national standards Speaking at SEC basketball media days last month, after the Protect College Sports Act advanced out of the Senate, Greg Sankey told CBS Sports the league would be ready for whichever direction the bill went . item.description: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images Even Todd Bowles has no idea what to expect from Buccaneers at trade deadline appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . On Sunday evening, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers dropped to 3-6 on the season with a tough road loss to the Chicago Bears in primetime. While the Buccaneers put up a good fight and were able to capitalize on several bizarre Chicago mistakes, they ultimately fell just short and squandered an opportunity to move into first place in the wretched NFC South. The NFL trade deadline is rapidly approaching later this week, and recently, Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles kept it one hundred percent honest about his thoughts on the team’s approach. “Bowles said the Bucs will listen to all calls at the trade deadline, both as buyers and sellers, but didn’t have a sense of which, if any, is more likely by Tuesday’s deadline,” reported Greg Auman of FOX Sports on X, formerly Twitter. On the one hand, the Buccaneers sit three games below the .500 mark on the season, and typically, teams with such a record aren’t necessarily viewed as buyers on the trade market. On the other hand, Tampa Bay recently knocked off two divisional opponents in blowout fashion and put together a still-impressive performance in Chicago despite the loss, meaning they are very much alive for the division title in the NFC South and could look to capitalize on their newfound momentum by adding some pieces. In the end, it will likely depend on the kind of offers the Buccaneers’ brass receives for some of their key players that determines what direction Tampa Bay chooses to go in. In any case, the Buccaneers will next hit the field on November 22 for a game vs the Detroit Lions following a bye week. item.title: Cardinals get brutal season-ending news on Michael Wilson amid neck fracture
item.description: Cardinals get brutal season-ending news on Michael Wilson amid neck fracture originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Arizona Cardinals have three wins in the 2026 NFL season, and aren't exactly playing great football. But part of the issue has been some horrible injury luck. Jeremiyah Love has missed a big chunk of the season, and they've also seen a few key linemen miss time. Kendrick Bourne is out for the season, and unfortunately, the hits keep coming for the Cardinals. According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , Michael Wilson is now out for the rest of the season after suffering a neck injury against the Seattle Seahawks in Week 9. Michael Wilson out for rest of 2026 after neck injury "Sources: AZCardinals WR Michael Wilson is out for the season after suffering a neck injury. Brutal," Rapoport reported. Not long after Rapoport's report, Cardinals' head coach Mike LaFleur revealed some shocking news about the neck injury. According to Josh Weinfuss of ESPN, the context of Wilson's neck injury makes it a lot more brutal for the WR. Not only was it a neck fracture, which is a scary-sounding injury, but Wilson actually suffered the injury on the fourth play of the game, didn't tell anyone, and played through a fractured neck for almost the entirety of the team's Week 9 loss. Wilson suffered a fractured neck on the fourth play of the game and wound up playing the remainder of the game for the Cardinals in an incredibly gutsy performance. MORE : Jaguars reportedly acquiring Falcons' Pro Bowl safety in major trade Of course, considering that this is a likely lost season for the Cardinals anyway, there is zero reason to try and bring Wilson back this season. After the Marvin Harrison Jr. trade, and both of the season-ending injuries to Wilson and Bourne, the Cardinals are now down to just Reggie Vergil, Simi Fehoko, Harrison Wallace III, and Devin Duvernay in their WR room. It would not be a surprise if the Cardinals made a move for some WR help, as their injuries have piled up to a ridiculous degree. Wilson will now miss the remainder of the season with a neck fracture that he initially played through. It's a brutal injury for the new $75 million WR. The next time the Cardinals see him, it will be in 2027, potentially with another new quarterback. item.description: Enzo Maresca's side lost their third consecutive Premier League game on Saturday -Credit:Lexy Ilsley, Manchester City FC via Getty Images Manchester City have been dealt another injury setback after Abdukodir Khusanov picked up a problem in the 3-1 loss to Nottingham Forest. The center-back finished the game at the City Ground but will miss Uzbekistan's upcoming friendlies against Russia and Saudi Arabia. The severity of Khusanov's injury remains unclear, but it adds to manager Enzo Maresca's concerns after two additional defenders requested substitutions at Forest. Marc Guéhi and Joško Gvardiol both experienced issues that led to their half-time withdrawals, while Nico O'Reilly has been omitted from the latest England squad after failing to reach full fitness throughout the season. Guéhi has subsequently withdrawn from the England squad, with Newcastle United's Dan Burn called up in his place. Meanwhile, it's uncertain whether Gvardiol will also pull out of Croatia duty, but Maresca must find stability at the back. Soccer star Jesús de Miguel tragically dies aged 30 after mid-game collision as tributes paid Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac address Wrexham executive’s abrupt exit -Credit:Andrew Kearns - CameraSport, CameraSport via Getty Images Elsewhere, Matheus Nunes has also battled injury concerns this campaign, with the team having conceded 17 goals across their last 8 matches, as per the Manchester Evening News . City suffered their third consecutive Premier League defeat with the loss at Forest - following losses to Brighton and Hove Albion and Aston Villa - to enter the latest international window on a disappointing note. Jair Cunha opened the scoring for Forest within six minutes, pouncing as Gvardiol was caught on the ball, with Liam Delap doubling their lead shortly after with a thundering run and shot. Rayan Cherki brought City back into the match with a top corner half-volley in the 52nd minute, before Morgan Gibbs-White and Delap combined to put the nail in the coffin via a deadly counter-attack with less than 20 minutes to go. Maresca acknowledged his team requires recovery time as he attempts to diagnose their slump in form before they resume action against Fulham a week on Saturday. item.title: Red Wings Playing Things Down to the Wire with Edvinsson
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Defenseman Simon Edvinsson remains unsigned through the first week of November, and the second month of the NHL season as the Detroit Red Wings find themselves floundering after a Halloween loss that seems to continue to haunt the team. The Red Wings could certainly use the big Swedish defenseman as they find themselves with a difficult schedule ahead against top Atlantic teams including the Florida Panthers, Tampa Bay Lightning, and Boston Bruins. For the moment, however, Edvinsson is still renting ice time in Nashville at the Predators’ facilities. Well, Simon Edvinsson is still here. pic.twitter.com/dc2SIkUZkY — Alex Daugherty (@AlexDaugherty1) November 9, 2026 According to the Lower Broad’s Nick Kieser, who met with Edvinsson in an unofficial capacity, Edvinsson came to the music city after Predators’ forward Filip Forsberg recommended a local skating coach, and “hopes to get something done soon.” Staring contest So far in the month and a half or so of Red Wings interim general manager Shawn Horcoff’ s tenure there has not appeared to be much movement in getting Edvinsson re-signed after the team failed to negotiate a contract for him before the end of training camp. On Oct. 30 TSN’s Darren Dreger reported that the Red Wings have submitted several contract offers to the Swedish blueliner at a variety of term lengths, but with the defenseman still skating in Nashville over the last week, it appears that progress towards pen to paper has stalled out. Insider Elliotte Friedman stated on a Friday appearance on NHL Now that Edvinsson was adamant about not wanting to play again in Detroit, however, that the Red Wings were willing to wait down until the Dec. 1 deadline to see if a deal can be done, much like Toronto did several years ago with William Nylander . “Right now there’s a lot of people who seem to think that the Red Wings will, if they want, if the Red Wings feel that ‘if we have to test him to see if his resolve is real’, they’ll do it.” Friedman said. Interestingly, the Predators will be visiting the Red Wings at home for Detroit’s last game of the month on Nov. 28 , two days before the Dec. 1 deadline to sign the defenseman for the season. Horcoff and the rest of the Detroit brass have been reportedly fending off potential trade partners with an exorbitant trade acquisition cost for Edvinsson in the meanwhile as they work to bring him back into the fold. item.description: Denis Poroy-Imagn Images Bob Nightengale just asking questions about possible Fernando Tatis Jr., Mason Miller trades appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The San Diego Padres could face difficult decisions this offseason as their new ownership group evaluates the franchise’s financial future. With several major contracts on the books and key players potentially attracting interest , trade speculation is beginning to surround Fernando Tatis Jr. and Mason Miller . In his latest USA Today column, Bob Nightengale discussed the uncertainty facing MLB teams ahead of a potential lockout and the possibility of more aggressive trade activity. Nightengale noted that executives would look to “coerce rivals into trades” during the general manager meetings. While that does not confirm the Padres are shopping either player, it has added to questions about how A.J. Preller could reshape the roster. Fernando Tatis Jr . would be a particularly difficult player to move. The 27-year-old remains one of baseball’s most dynamic talents, combining power, speed and defensive versatility. He also has eight years and approximately $266 million remaining on his contract, along with a full no-trade clause through 2028. Any potential deal would require his approval and a significant return for San Diego. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Mason Miller could also attract attention after establishing himself as one of the game’s premier relief pitchers. He recorded 38 saves and 129 strikeouts in 2026, making him a valuable asset for a contender seeking late-inning help. The Padres would likely demand a substantial prospect package before considering such a move. The St. Louis Cardinals could emerge as an intriguing hypothetical destination for Tatis. His father, Fernando Tatis Sr., previously played for St. Louis, while the Cardinals have young talent and financial flexibility to explore a major acquisition. However, there is no confirmed link between the two sides. For now, the Padres’ plans remain unclear. Any decision involving Tatis or Miller would depend on the new ownership group’s direction and Preller’s assessment of the team’s future. item.description: Michigan State’s path to bowl eligibility now comes down to three games. The Spartans sit at 3-6 and have to win all three to get to the six wins a bowl requires, starting Saturday at home against Washington, with No. 23 Oregon and Rutgers after that. That math only exists because of Saturday night in Ann Arbor. After Michigan State beat Michigan 15-6, bringing Paul Bunyan back to East Lansing for the first time since 2021 , the Spartans snapped a six-game losing streak and gave themselves something to play for in November. Pat Fitzgerald spoke to the media Monday in a video posted by Spartan Mag about where that bowl goal sits. Michigan State Bowl Eligibility Starts With Washington Fitzgerald did not spend long on the big picture, and he did not pretend it was not there either. “Talked about the macro for about eight seconds this morning in a team meeting, and close that drawer up pretty quickly, but I like having motivation in November,” Fitzgerald said. He was more direct about what the three games could buy his roster. “There’s no doubt there’s an opportunity if we do what we’re capable of to create an extra month with our seniors,” Fitzgerald said, per the Detroit News . Bowl eligibility would be Michigan State’s first since 2021. For now, his message to the team stops at Washington. “We all know that, that win you know gave us an opportunity, and the right to have this be a big game this weekend,” Fitzgerald said. “That’s the way I’ve approached it with the guys, this is a critical game for this team. You know I said, listen, then that creates next week and the week after; we’ll worry about them down the road.” The Players Proved They Could Execute The Game Plan Pat Fitzgerald said his players came to him to point out their mistakes after the 28-10 loss to UCLA , and they used the bye week to lock back in. He talked about the disappointing second half, which saw UCLA score touchdowns on their first two drives , while the Spartans offense went three-and-out twice. item.title: Jets’ Scott Arniel reveals ‘hard’ part of Connor Hellebuyck not starting in Devils clash
item.description: Nick Turchiaro-Imagn Images Jets’ Scott Arniel reveals ‘hard’ part of Connor Hellebuyck not starting in Devils clash appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Winnipeg Jets will welcome the New Jersey Devils to Canada Life Centre on Tuesday night for the first time since the Connor Hellebuyck trade — but almost inexplicably, the 33-year-old will not be between the pipes for the contest. Instead, the Devils will turn to Jake Allen, while Hellebuyck , who spent the first 11 years of his career in Manitoba, will watch from the bench. The decision has drawn sharp criticism from across the hockey world, and Jets head coach Scott Arniel chimed in on Monday. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “It goes back to the ownership, it goes back to the fans, it goes back to the core guys that have been with Helly from the very beginning, who he kind of left on,” the bench boss told reporters, per TSN. “That’s the part for me that’s hard, he just gave up on us, and so it would be nice to just finally be done with this. All it does is drag it out 10 or nine more games from now, we’re going to have to start into it and talk about it again here. That’s the biggest disappointment.” Jets head coach Scott Arniel shares his thoughts on Connor Hellebuyck not starting in his return to Winnipeg. pic.twitter.com/fSBrsqTvRl — TSN (@TSN_Sports) November 9, 2026 The Jets and Devils will play for the second and final time in 2026-27 on Nov. 28 in Newark. New Jersey general manager Sunny Mehta announced the decision Sunday, and Hellebuyck also shared his thoughts , saying he was disappointed he wouldn’t be starting. “We definitely had a conversation and I told them my thoughts on it and they told me theirs, and at the end of the day I have to listen to them and I can only push so hard,” Hellebuyck said. “I can only push so hard. I was adamant that I want to play, but it is what it is.” Mehta said that starting Hellebuyck on Tuesday “would potentially give us a reduction in our expected win probability,” an explanation that has drawn widespread criticism . Hellebuyck is 5-0-0 with a 1.96 goals-against average and .913 save percentage with the Devils, and he just shut out the Toronto Maple Leafs on Sunday. Meanwhile, Allen sports a 3.20 goals-against average and .881 save percentage. It’s a bad look for the Devils, who should have let Hellebuyck face the music and move on. Instead, they’ve prolonged the storyline until the teams meet again at the end of the month — with no guarantee he’ll start that game, either.

item.title: St. Louis Cardinals Interested in Reunion With World Series Champion
item.description: MIAMI, FLORIDA - JULY 6: Oliver Marmol #37 of the St. Louis Cardinals looks on prior to the game against the Miami Marlins at loanDepot park on July 6, 2023 in Miami, Florida. (Photo by Sam Navarro/Getty Images) Getty The St. Louis Cardinals traded away starter Dustin May and reliever JoJo Romero to the Milwaukee Brewers at the Trade Deadline in a fire sale. Those two players would win a World Series with Milwaukee, becoming key contributors. Now, both will hit free agency. May’s market is likely cold after how he finished the year, but Romero’s could be hot. According to Derrick Goold of the St. Louis Dispatch, the Cardinals are considering a reunion with Romero. The left-handed reliever recorded a 3.36 ERA in 2026 between St. Louis and Milwaukee. Should The Cardinals Bring Back Romero? The Philadelphia Phillies drafted Romero in the fourth round of the 2016 MLB Draft out of Yavapai College. He debuted with Philadelphia during the COVID-shortened 2020 season with horrible results. In 25 games over three seasons with the Phillies, Romero recorded a 7.89 ERA. Philadelphia traded him to St. Louis in exchange for utility man Edmundo Sosa in 2022. He finished out that season with St. Louis, recording a 3.77 ERA in 15 games, a glimpse of what was to come. In 2023, he recorded a 3.68 ERA in 27 games. The 2024 season would be his breakout year, with Romero posting a 3.36 ERA in 65 games. He followed that up with a stellar 2.07 ERA in 65 games during the 2025 season. So, over five seasons with St. Louis, Romero had a 3.07 ERA in 216 games. He was a part of the stellar Milwaukee bullpen that dominated in the postseason. In seven playoff appearances, Romero posted a 1.13 ERA. Entering his age-31 season, Romero should be one of the more highly sought-after free agents in this class. With his familiarity in St. Louis, it wouldn’t be surprising at all if the team seeks a reunion. State Of the Team’s Bullpen While the Cardinals desperately need pitching, does it make sense to add during a mini-rebuild? Riley O’Brien is set to be the closer for St. Louis again despite blowing eight saves in 2026. After O’Brien, there isn’t a clear plan for who should be the setup man. Justin Bruihl pitched in a team-high 73 games in 2026, recording a 3.59 ERA. Gordon Graceffo pitched in 62 games with a 2.67 ERA. Both of those arms should be considered for the eighth-inning role. However, Romero has been the more consistent and experienced arm during his career and would fit in rather nicely in the Cardinals bullpen. George Soriano, Max Rajcic, Luis Gastelum, Hancel Rincon, Cade Winquest and Brycen Mautz, among others, will fight for roles in the bullpen. The Cardinals bullpen was one of the worst in baseball, with a 4.51 ERA. If they reunite with Romero, they have a solid chance of improving that number. item.title: Sabres Quietly Have One of NHL’s Best Players
item.description: Getty Getty Getty Getty After shocking the NHL last season by finishing tops in the Eastern Conference, the Buffalo Sabres have experienced a mini-hangover in 2026-27. Starting netminder Ukko-Pekka Lukkonen has struggled. So have players like Josh Norris and Josh Doan. Overall, Buffalo is 21st overall in goals scored, middle of the pack in terms of goals against, and their special teams play has been subpar. However, one of their young forwards is quietly putting together a dominant campaign. Zach Benson’s Underlying Numbers Stack Up With the NHL’s Best Zach Benson isn’t necessarily the first name that comes to mind when discussing the league’s most impactful forwards. But, a closer look at his underlying numbers suggests he’s becoming an extremely valuable player in Buffalo. The 21-year-old winger has quietly put together an impressive start to the 2026-27 campaign, recording 15 points (2 goals, 13 assists) through his first 17 games. While those numbers don’t scream ‘superstar,’ his underlying metrics paint a different picture. The Sabres have controlled 62.1 per cent of shot attempts with Benson on the ice so far this season. That total ranks sixth-best among all NHLers, behind only four Carolina Hurricanes players and Jack Hughes. Buffalo controlling shots to that degree with Benson on the ice is even more compelling when you consider that, as a team, they’re controlling less than 50% of shot attempts at five-on-five. Benson’s shot-attempt differential relative to his team is +13.1 per cent. The only NHLers who are better are Artemi Panarin and four members of the top-heavy Edmonton Oilers (Connor McDavid, Leon Draisaitl, Vasily Podkolzin and Evan Bouchard). item.description: Magomed Ankalaev Getty Former UFC light heavyweight champion Magomed Ankalaev said that he is frustrated that no one wants to step into the Octagon with him. Ankalaev has not competed since UFC Abu Dhabi in July, when he scored a fifth-round TKO win over Bogdan Guskov. But despite wanting to fight, no one has stepped up to the plate and challenged the former champ yet. Magomed Ankalaev Frustrated By Inactivity Taking to his social media on Monday, Ankalaev let loose his frustrations about the fact he is not fighting anyone right now. “Looks like nobody in the top five at light heavyweight wants to fight. Everybody’s got a reason. Khalil Rountree not ready Reyes just fought and is injured. Costa wants $10 million. So what about heavyweight? Anybody ready to fight? So, we’ll see what the UFC ends up doing with Ankalaev. He’s clearly one of the best light heavyweights in the sport today, but for whatever reason, he is having difficulties getting a fight booked. Hopefully, someone will step up to the plate soon and fight Ankalaev so we can get this UFC Dallas main event with Ankalaev as the headliner booked sooner rather than later. Zack Kelly is moving on from the Boston Red Sox after five seasons in the organization, but the right-handed reliever made sure to acknowledge his time with the club. Kelly shared a farewell message on social media Sunday, thanking the Red Sox organization, his former teammates and Boston fans following his release. What a ride! I’m grateful to have been a part of such a historic organization the last 6 years. Playing at Fenway Park was incredible and something I never took for granted. Thank you to the organization, my teammates, and the fans for being behind us every single night. Looking forward to the next chapter ⚾️ — Zack Kelly (@zack_kelly) November 9, 2026 “What a ride! I’m grateful to have been a part of such a historic organization the last 6 years,” Kelly wrote on X. “Playing at Fenway Park was incredible and something I never took for granted. Thank you to the organization, my teammates, and the fans for being behind us every single night. Looking forward to the next chapter.” The Red Sox officially released Kelly on Nov. 9 after designating him for assignment on Nov. 2 . He cleared waivers before becoming a free agent, bringing his time in Boston to an end. Boston originally signed Kelly to a minor-league contract in 2021 . He made his major-league debut with the Red Sox on Aug. 29, 2022, and went on to appear in 115 games across five seasons with the club. Kelly finished his Boston tenure with an 8-8 record and a 4.04 ERA across 131 1/3 innings. He recorded 127 strikeouts during that span. The 2026 season showed promise before an injury cut his campaign short. Kelly posted a 3.31 ERA with 14 strikeouts across 17 appearances, going 0-2. The 31-year-old last pitched in the majors on July 3 before an elbow injury sidelined him for the remainder of the season. Boston placed him on the 60-day injured list in July with right elbow inflammation. Kelly will now look for his next opportunity elsewhere as he enters free agency.
